sections.这一篇讲什么:
**Changing a prompt without measuring is just guessing in a different way.**
There are four routes to iteration: manual comparison, meta-prompting, automated search, and runtime generate-evaluate loops.
Automation increases along the list, and human judgment shifts from wording to criteria.
We have not run hands-on tests; the mechanisms below come from official tutorials and papers.
sections.人工迭代：基线对比:
OpenAI's meta-prompting cookbook demonstrates the full workflow:
write a simple prompt as the baseline, generate an enhanced version,
run both over the same dataset, and score them item by item against predefined criteria.
The key to comparison is controlled variables: inputs and scoring stay fixed, so differences attribute to the prompt.

The cookbook's scoring method is an LLM judge:
a model compares the two outputs against criteria such as accuracy, clarity, and relevance.
Without this step, "feels better" is an impression, not a conclusion.
sections.元提示：让模型改提示词:
Meta-prompting's definition: using an LLM to generate or improve prompts.
The typical setup in OpenAI's cookbook: a stronger model optimizes prompts for a weaker one.
Feed the optimizer context and goals so it can produce a targeted enhancement.

A labor-saving detail: the judge prompt used for scoring can itself be meta-optimized.
The iteration method applies to itself.
The cost: an extra optimizer call, and whether the enhanced version is actually better still requires running the comparison.
sections.自动搜索：APE:
The APE paper treats instructions as "programs" to be synthesized:
an LLM proposes a pool of candidate instructions, search maximizes a chosen score function over them,
and another LLM's zero-shot performance evaluates the selected instruction.
The paper reports: across 24 NLP tasks, automatically generated instructions beat the zero-shot baseline by a large margin,
matching or exceeding human-annotated instructions on 19 of 24 (the paper's own report, not our testing).

The mechanical point: the score function decides the search direction.
If the score is misdefined, the selected instruction is misaligned — settle the criteria before searching.
sections.运行时循环：生成器与评估器:
Anthropic's evaluator-optimizer pattern moves iteration to runtime:
a generator produces an answer; an evaluator judges without solving, returning PASS / NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT / FAIL plus feedback;
on failure, the generator regenerates with previous attempts and feedback until it passes.
In the reference implementation, the evaluator is explicitly told to evaluate only, never attempt the task,
and outputs use XML tags so code can branch on them.

Note: the reference implementation loops until PASS with no iteration cap.
Production needs its own step limit and fallback exit (our view).
sections.失败模式:
1. No baseline: the change feels better but was never compared. Run the baseline first.
2. Misaligned criteria: a score function or judge standard that misses the real goal optimizes you further off course.
3. Shared blind spots: when evaluator and generator are the same kind of model, they may share the same blind spots (our view).
4. Non-convergence: a generate-evaluate loop with no cap burns tokens without ever passing.
5. Small-sample overfitting: optimizing against a few examples makes the prompt memorize them instead of learning the task (our view).

The shared premise of all four routes: define what "good" means first, then let any mechanism approach it.
